criteria.description: Correctly applies the Taylor expansion at t=t_k.
Correctly substitutes the ODE xdot=f(x,t) in place of the derivative.
Correctly relabels as the iterated update rule x_{k+1} = x_k + h*f(x_k,t_k).

solutions.fullSolution: x(t_k+h) ~= x(t_k) + h*xdot(t_k) (Taylor expansion at t_k). Substituting xdot(t_k)=f(x(t_k),t_k): x(t_k+h) ~= x(t_k) + h*f(x(t_k),t_k). Writing x_k for the numerical approximation of x(t_k) and x_{k+1} for x(t_k+h): x_{k+1} = x_k + h*f(x_k,t_k), the forward Euler update, i.e. Euler is literally 'take one first-order Taylor step, then repeat.'

0.10653/0.00024 ~= 443.9 (using the precise values from the worked examples, 0.10653065971263342/0.00024017362069994608 = 443.5568..., rounds to about 443.6). Verified with NumPy while authoring this module. RK4's error here is over 400x smaller than Euler's for the same step size, at only 4x the per-step cost.
